title: EC2 Instances and Storage
description: Learn about EBS volume types, snapshots, encryption, Elastic IPs, and Spot Instances.

data.text: EC2 instances need persistent storage. Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) provides block-level storage volumes that you can attach to EC2 instances. EBS volumes persist independently from the life of an instance, so your data remains even if the instance is stopped or terminated.

EBS snapshots are incremental backups of your volumes stored in Amazon S3. You can restore a snapshot to create a new volume or copy it to another Region for disaster recovery. EBS encryption is built in and uses AWS Key Management Service (KMS) to protect your data at rest and in transit.

An Elastic IP address is a static IPv4 address designed for dynamic cloud computing. You can allocate an Elastic IP to your account and associate it with an EC2 instance or a network interface. This ensures your instance keeps the same public IP address even if you stop and start it.

Spot Instances let you use unused EC2 capacity at steep discounts. AWS sets the Spot price based on supply and demand. If the price exceeds your bid or capacity is needed, AWS terminates the instance with a two-minute warning. Spot Instances are perfect for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads like batch processing.

terms.definition: A durable block storage device that can be attached to an EC2 instance.
An incremental backup of an EBS volume stored in Amazon S3.
A static public IP address you can allocate and attach to your instances.
An EC2 instance offered at a discounted price using unused AWS capacity.

data.title: Create and Attach an EBS Volume
data.content: This AWS CLI example creates a 20 GB gp3 volume, attaches it to an instance, and takes a snapshot.
data.code:
# Create a 20 GB gp3 volume in us-east-1a
aws ec2 create-volume \
  --volume-type gp3 \
  --size 20 \
  --availability-zone us-east-1a \
  --encrypted

# Attach the volume to an instance
aws ec2 attach-volume \
  --volume-id vol-1234567890abcdef0 \
  --instance-id i-1234567890abcdef0 \
  --device /dev/sdf

# Create a snapshot of the volume
aws ec2 create-snapshot \
  --volume-id vol-1234567890abcdef0 \
  --description "Backup of my EBS volume"

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: EBS provides persistent block storage for EC2 instances
gp3 volumes offer the best price and performance for general workloads
Snapshots provide incremental backups stored in S3
EBS encryption protects data at rest using KMS
Elastic IPs provide static public IP addresses
Spot Instances offer significant discounts for flexible workloads
